messages.content: I’m at the cutoff on the San Diego hotels. I was leaning split stay like you suggested, but I need the final go/no-go before I touch the bayfront booking.

Go split unless the bayfront weekend reprices badly. The downtown block solves the two painful work mornings and Thursday teardown. The bayfront still protects the weekend with Matt, and you avoid paying bayfront rates for nights when the hot tub is unavailable anyway. The trade-off is one repack and Friday bag handling.

Here are the details I got: downtown block is open Monday through Thursday nights, Friday checkout, $219 plus tax, cancellation until 72 hours before arrival. Bayfront can shorten to Friday and Saturday nights at $286 a night. They said the balcony request can be re-added but not guaranteed. Matt still lands Friday at 3:30.

That supports the split. Book downtown Monday Jan. 27 through Friday Jan. 31 checkout first, then modify bayfront to Friday Jan. 31 through Sunday Feb. 2 checkout. Keep the king room request, high floor, and balcony note on the bayfront reservation. Do not cancel the bayfront until the shortened reservation shows the Friday/Saturday rate and the same confirmation or a new valid confirmation.
My only hesitation is repacking Friday. The CE session may run until noon, and I don’t want to drag the roller bag into the convention center.

Use the downtown bell desk. Pack Thursday night, check out Friday morning before the CE session, leave the roller bag and expo tote at the hotel, then rideshare to the bayfront after lunch. If the bayfront room is not ready, drop bags there and meet Matt at the hotel instead of the airport.
Will the hot tub reopening Friday afternoon change anything? They still won’t promise a time.

It should not change the lodging decision. Ask them to note that you are arriving Friday for a weekend stay and want confirmation of pool, hot tub, and fitness hours the day before. If the hot tub slips to Friday evening, you still have Saturday; if it slips past Saturday, then it becomes a service issue to ask about at check-in.
Okay. What exact confirmations do I need before I let the long bayfront stay go?

In order: 1) downtown confirmation number for Monday through Thursday nights, Friday checkout; 2) downtown cancellation deadline in writing; 3) bayfront shortened dates and total price; 4) confirmation that shortening does not trigger a penalty or lose the king-room category; 5) balcony/high-floor request copied onto the shortened stay; 6) Friday bag storage or early bag drop noted at both hotels if possible.
Downtown just confirmed fitness access and early bag drop, but no pool or hot tub. I can live with that for the work part. Bayfront says the price only goes up about $38 total after the change.

Then proceed with the split. The $38 difference is worth the walkable Wednesday breakfast and easier teardown. Leave the flights alone, keep rideshares as the plan, and put a Friday luggage reminder on your calendar for both checkout and bayfront check-in.
Give me the finance line and a quick note for Matt so I can close this out.

Finance line: lodging changed to the convention block Monday through Thursday nights to reduce early expo transportation and teardown risk; personal weekend lodging remains Friday and Saturday at the bayfront, with no flight changes and no rental car added. Note for Matt: fly in Friday as booked, rideshare straight to the bayfront, and I’ll transfer bags after my CE session unless the room is ready earlier.

messages.content: Five days out from San Diego. The split stay is done. Can you run the final logistics pass so I don’t miss anything?

Yes. Monday: leave for DEN around 9:45 to 10:00 for the 12:45 p.m. nonstop, land SAN 2:11, rideshare to the downtown hotel, drop bags if the room is not ready, then check the booth area before dinner. Wednesday breakfast is walkable from downtown. Thursday teardown stays downtown-friendly. Friday is the only moving part.
Friday is what I’m worried about. Matt lands at 3:30, my CE session may go until noon, and downtown checkout is 11.

Cleanest version: check out before the CE session, leave bags with the downtown bell desk, finish CE, grab bags, rideshare to the bayfront around 12:30 or 1:00, and ask for pre-check. Matt should rideshare directly from SAN to the bayfront; airport pickup adds waiting and traffic without much benefit.
Good. The bayfront still says balcony request only.

Call the bayfront Thursday afternoon and again Friday morning if needed. Ask them to keep the king, high-floor, balcony request attached to the shortened stay and to confirm pool/hot tub timing. I would not prepay a big upgrade unless they can guarantee the room type.
What about seats and the Sunday return?

Check Erin’s Monday seat map at check-in and keep a window if one is open. For Sunday, review both tickets together and keep paired seats on the 1:50 p.m. SAN-DEN return. Plan to leave the bayfront around 11:10 or 11:15 unless brunch runs long.
Give me the reminders to add.

Add these: Sunday morning check in for Erin’s Monday flight; Monday pack booth badge and charger separately from checked luggage; Thursday call bayfront about balcony and hot tub; Friday 7:30 a.m. downtown checkout and bell-desk bag drop; Friday 12:30 p.m. bag pickup and rideshare to bayfront; Friday 3:30 p.m. Matt lands and goes straight to hotel; Saturday decide only then whether a one-day car is worth it; Sunday 11:15 a.m. depart for SAN.

messages.content: San Diego is done, and now I have Kansas City coming at me. It’s an early-spring lab training week, probably the week of March 17. I need a flight, hotel area, and rental car plan before I send anything to finance.
I can help. What do you know so far: which clinics or lab sites, whether Monday is actually in person, and whether you are carrying equipment or shipping it?

Expected stops are Overland Park, Lenexa, and North Kansas City. Tuesday through Thursday trainings are likely, but Monday calibration may become in-person. I may have the demo analyzer case plus workbook cartons if the kits don’t ship cleanly. Parking and unloading matter more than restaurants. If Sunday is the right answer, I’d rather leave Denver after lunch than take a dawn flight.

Given that, I would plan around Sunday arrival unless Monday is officially remote. It buys time for a calibration, lets you inspect shipped kits, and avoids starting the week with equipment stress. Hotel-wise, Overland Park looks like the best base unless North Kansas City becomes the first or longest day.
Finance will ask why I’m adding Sunday night if Monday isn’t confirmed yet.

Frame Sunday as a risk-control hold, not extra comfort. The justification is: possible Monday in-person calibration, equipment handling, and multiple suburban sites. If Monday is confirmed remote and all kits are delivered by the prior Friday, you can release the Sunday night and switch to a Monday morning arrival.
Give me actual flight targets. Keep connections simple. If a United nonstop is close, that’s fine, but don’t pick it over a cleaner schedule.

Flight ranking for now: first, Sunday Mar. 16 afternoon DEN-MCI nonstop, ideally early-to-mid afternoon so you arrive with daylight to pick up the car and unload. United or Southwest would both be fine if the times and baggage rules work. Second, Monday morning nonstop only if calibration is remote and kits are already delivered. Third, any connecting itinerary is not worth it for this route unless nonstops disappear or pricing gets unusually bad.
Return day is fuzzy. There may be a Friday morning debrief, but Thursday could be the last clinic.

Hold the return as Friday afternoon if finance allows. If the debrief drops, move to a Thursday evening nonstop after the North Kansas City session. I would avoid a tight Thursday departure unless you know teardown, case packing, and the drive back from North Kansas City will be done by midafternoon.

Hotels I’m seeing: an Overland Park suite property with good reviews, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness; a Plaza business hotel with better dinner options but paid parking and fewer amenities; and an airport hotel.

Rank them this way: 1) Overland Park suite property, because it matches the suburban training pattern, free parking, and recovery amenities while keeping Lenexa easy. 2) Plaza business hotel, only if evening meals or a client dinner become the priority; paid parking and weaker amenities are drawbacks with equipment. 3) Airport hotel, useful for arrival only, but it creates repeated cross-town drives on clinic days.
The Overland Park one is rated about 4.4 on Google. Plaza is 4.1, airport is 4.0-ish. I’d rather not go below that if we have workable choices.

Then the Overland Park suite property stays clearly first. It is the best mix of review strength, parking, pool, hot tub, fitness, and drive pattern. The Plaza option is acceptable but less practical. The airport option is more of a fallback if the first night becomes very late or the suburban hotels sell out.
Is Overland Park still logical for North Kansas City day? I don’t want to set myself up for a horrible commute.

It is manageable as one longer day, especially if North Kansas City is only Thursday. Expect roughly 30 to 45 minutes depending on timing. If North Kansas City becomes two days or the first morning starts early, then reconsider a split or a hotel farther north. With one NKC day, I would not move hotels.
Rental car: sedan or small SUV? The analyzer case is basically a chunky Pelican case, plus two cartons if shipping fails.

Book a small or midsize SUV. The hatch and fold-down rear seats matter more than passenger space. Avoid a compact sedan because the trunk opening can become the problem. At pickup, check that the case can lie flat and that you have a cargo cover or can bring equipment into the hotel overnight.
If the kits ship directly and Monday calibration goes remote, could I still salvage a Monday morning flight?

Yes, but only if three things are true by the prior Friday: Monday is confirmed remote, the kits are delivered or signed for at the first site, and Tuesday’s first training does not require a same-day setup visit. If any one of those is uncertain, Sunday afternoon remains the safer plan.
What about Lenexa instead of Overland Park?

Lenexa is a good backup if the first two training days land west or if the hotel rate is meaningfully better. I still prefer Overland Park because it has the stronger amenity fit and sits well for both Overland Park and Lenexa while keeping the North Kansas City day tolerable.
Give me a finance-ready summary and what I should wait on before booking.

Finance summary: recommended hold is Sunday Mar. 16 afternoon DEN-MCI nonstop, Friday Mar. 21 afternoon return, Overland Park suite hotel Sunday through Thursday nights with free parking and pool/hot tub/fitness, and a small or midsize SUV for equipment transport. Rationale: protects possible Monday calibration, reduces equipment-delivery risk, and keeps the three-site clinic pattern efficient. Wait on: Monday calibration decision, final clinic order, Friday debrief yes/no, shipped-kit tracking and delivery address, and hotel parking/loading details.
Assume I can put a 24-hour hold on the flight and a cancellable hotel. What should I hold now?

Hold the Sunday afternoon nonstop to MCI, Friday afternoon return, the Overland Park suite property for Sunday through Thursday nights on a cancellable rate, and a small or midsize SUV from MCI. Put a review reminder for next week: if Monday becomes remote and kits are confirmed delivered, switch to Monday morning and drop Sunday night; if Friday debrief disappears, move the return to Thursday evening.
